title: Glider-borne automated whale-call classifier triggers a NOAA Right Whale Slow Zone east of Portland, Maine
summary: WHOI/NOAA glider's automated call classifier detected right whales on 27 December 2023; NOAA declared a Slow Zone east of Portland, ME.
account: On 27 December 2023 the Gulf of Maine Winter Slocum glider, operated by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and NOAA's Northeast Fisheries Science Center, acoustically detected North Atlantic right whales east of Portland, Maine. Such gliders carry a DMON instrument running the Low-Frequency Detection and Classification System, which matches pitch-tracked calls against a call library using quadratic discriminant function analysis; shore-based analysts validate detections. On 29 December 2023 NOAA Fisheries announced a voluntary Right Whale Slow Zone bounded by 43°49'N, 43°09'N, 67°02'W and 68°57'W, effective 27 December 2023 through 11 January 2024, requesting that mariners route around the area or transit at 10 knots or less.
purpose: LFDCS was built to detect and classify baleen whale calls in near real time for management use; the Slow Zone trigger was that purpose.
system: DMON instrument running the Low-Frequency Detection and Classification System (LFDCS) on a Slocum glider
deployer: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and NOAA Northeast Fisheries Science Center; NOAA Fisheries issues Slow Zones
location: Gulf of Maine east of Portland, United States

ratings.reason: A protective speed-reduction request for an endangered species over a defined area for about 15 days; no evidence that a strike was averted or that specific vessels complied.

ai_role.statement: Automated classification produced the candidate detections; analysts validated them on shore before NOAA acted; the resulting Slow Zone is voluntary.

paired_incident.title: Poachers Evaded AI Cameras and Killed Four Rhinos
paired_incident.basis: Automated detection to protect an endangered species: the glider's whale-call classifier triggered a ship Slow Zone, while Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife's AI cameras failed to detect poachers and four rhinos were killed.

headline: LFDCS glider detections trigger a NOAA Right Whale Slow Zone
metric: mariners route around the area or transit at 10 knots or less

comparator.after: more slowdowns than aerial surveillance by a factor of two to five during fall and summer
comparator.quote: Gliders triggered more slowdowns than aerial surveillance by a factor of two to five during fall and summer but were less effective during spring, as whales migrating into the GoSL tend to call at lower rates and occur at lower densities than during other behavioral states (Parks et al., 2011; Matthews and Parks, 2021).

later.note: By early 2025 gliders had triggered or extended 51 of the 154 acoustically triggered Slow Zones, and on 20 January 2024 a glider made the first definite glider-based acoustic detection in southeast US waters.
later.quote: In the four years since its inception, 154 Slow Zones have been triggered or extended by acoustic detections of NARWs, and 51 (33%) of those Slow Zones were triggered or extended by gliders operated by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Rutgers University, Stony Brook University, and The University of Maine during 57 separate glider missions.
